papers.title_in_file: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm in Finite Size and Large Depth and Equivalence to Quantum Annealing
papers.version_note: arXiv:2503.09563v2 (8 Oct 2025); text matches the record.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proving that QAOA with angles discretized from a smooth schedule of bounded total gamma approximates the energy of linear-time quantum annealing on the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, with numerical tests at optimized angles.

existing.note: The abstract states the two conditions loosely. The paper proves the result only for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, for the disorder-averaged energy density, with a Lipschitz continuous gamma schedule and the maximum gamma below an absolute constant (Theorem III.4).
existing.value: The authors state that QAOA energy approximates that of quantum annealing under two conditions, namely that angles vary smoothly from one layer to the next and that the sum is bounded by a constant. The paper proves this for the disorder-average of the energy density of QAOA on the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model, for angles discretized from a bounded schedule with a Lipschitz continuous gamma schedule.
quotes: we provide evidence against this by analytically showing that QAOA energy approximates that of quantum annealing under two conditions, namely that angles vary smoothly from one layer to the next and that the sum is bounded by a constant.
More precisely, we prove this equivalence result for the disorder-average of the energy density achieved by QAOA on the SherringtonKirkpatrick (SK) model.

existing.certainty_reason: Abstract, Section I and Theorem III.4 state the proved result and its conditions.
existing.reader_inference: The abstract's phrase 'smoothly' corresponds to a Lipschitz continuous gamma schedule; the 'sum bounded by a constant' corresponds to the maximum gamma below an absolute constant.

existing.note: The proof needs more than 'angles smaller than an absolute constant'. Theorem III.4 requires angles discretized from a bounded continuous schedule with a Lipschitz gamma, and Eq. 32 shows the total gamma angle is then bounded by an absolute constant. The error bound is stated with a constant that depends on the schedule, and the numerical evidence shows the equivalence is not captured at exactly optimized angles.
existing.value: The authors prove that if the angles are smaller than an absolute constant independent of the instance size, QAOA achieves energy density arbitrarily close to that of quantum annealing with corresponding schedule for sufficiently large depth, for the disorder-average on the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. The theorem assumes angles that come from the discretization of a fixed bounded continuous schedule whose gamma part is Lipschitz, and requires the maximum gamma to be below an absolute constant.

assertions.value: The authors state that the standard analysis of Trotter error, which approximates the evolution operator in operator norm, can be applied to QAOA only for angles of order one over n, and so does not interpret QAOA with constant angles as a Trotterization of annealing.
assertions.anchor: Section III D, text-layer page 16
quotes: All in all, the standard analysis of Trotter error, aimed at approximating the Hamiltonian evolution operator in operator norm, may only be applied to QAOA for angles of order 1/n.
Hence, the standard analysis of Trotter does not allow to interpret QAOA as a Trotterization of the adiabatic algorithm
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived in Section III D from the Trotter bound and the norm scaling of the Hamiltonians.
assertions.reader_inference: The statement concerns the standard bound, not a lower bound proof that no other analysis can work.

assertions.value: The paper states Corollary III.5: under the conditions of Theorem III.4, for every positive epsilon there is a circuit of depth order n over epsilon that outputs an energy epsilon-close to the annealing energy with high probability over the SK instance, a quadratic improvement in n over the depth required by the standard Trotter analysis.
assertions.anchor: Corollary III.5, Section III E, text-layer page 16
quotes: Corollary III.5 (Quadratic depth reduction in Trotterization of SK model annealing).
Assume, as in the statement of Theorem III.4 (equation 30), that the maximum of γcont and the total continuous γ angles are bounded by absolute constants.
Then, for all ε > 0, there exists a circuit of depth O (n/ε) outputting an energy εclose to the energy of the annealing evolution with high probability over the random choice of SK instance.
Consequently, the standard analysis of Trotter error and theorem III.4 respectively require a circuit of depth n2 and n/ε.
assertions.certainty_reason: Corollary III.5 with a short proof from Theorem III.4 and the depth of each SK layer.
assertions.reader_inference: The depth of n per layer rests on all-to-all connectivity, as the proof states.

assertions.value: The authors state that their theory does not predict how the Trotter step size varies with total evolution time, that the proportionality constant may need to decrease with the total evolution time, and that numerical results suggest it can be increased.
assertions.anchor: Sections III E and IV, text-layer page 16
quotes: In particular, it is theoretically possible that the proportionality constant in the linearly growing Trotter step size must decrease with the total evolution time, rendering the improvement less favorable for large total evolution time.

Unfortunately, our theoretical results fall short of predicting how the Trotter step size varies as a function of the total evolution time, though numerical results seem to show it can actually be increased with total evolution time.
assertions.certainty_reason: Sections III E and IV state the limit.

assertions.value: The authors state that their proof techniques are restricted to the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model and constant total evolution time, and that they expect the results to generalize broadly.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing earlier work, that QAOA with small angles of order one over n can provably recover the quantum adiabatic algorithm, and that optimal QAOA angles were observed to be of constant order for a broad family of problems.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing earlier work, that efficient classical algorithms exist for approximate solutions of the SK model when the error is independent of n, and that the ratio between QAOA energy and the optimal energy is empirically conjectured to reach one as the number of layers goes to infinity.

assertions.value: The authors report that the numerical experiments use SK instances of 20 spins in the performance diagram and sizes from 10 to 20 in the additional scans, start from infinite-size optimized angles for p equal to 17 taken from earlier work, and extrapolate them to larger p by a Fourier procedure.

assertions.value: The authors report that for constant total evolution time the difference between the QAOA and annealing energies decreases with p, that the decay matches order one over p as predicted by the theorem, and that there is no dependence on n.

assertions.value: The paper defines the relative residual approximation ratio as the QAOA approximation ratio minus the annealing approximation ratio, divided by one minus the annealing approximation ratio, and uses it because both algorithms may approach the exact solution.
